instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.62(10) defines lobbying as attempting to influence legislative or administrative action by oral/written communication with officials, and includes time spent in preparation, appearances at public hearings or meetings, and committee service in which such preparation or communication occurs.

Section 13.62(11) defines a lobbyist as an individual employed by a principal, or who contracts for or receives economic consideration (other than expense reimbursement) from a principal, whose duties include lobbying.

Section 13.62(2) defines "agency" as any board, commission, department, office, society, institution of higher education, council, or committee in the state government, plus certain enumerated authorities — this is a defined public entity term.

Section 13.62(11) imposes a 5-day-per-reporting-period threshold for individuals whose duties are not exclusively lobbying, and §13.64(1) imposes a $500 aggregate expenditure threshold for principal registration — both are materiality/de minimis tests.

Section 13.62(10) defines lobbying to include communication with agency officials, and §13.62(2)-(3) define "agency" to include state departments/boards/commissions and "agency official" as one participating in administrative action, covering executive agencies.

Section 13.62(3) defines "agency official" to include any member, officer, employee, or consultant of any agency who participates in administrative action in other than a solely clerical/secretarial/ministerial capacity — covering executive branch staff.

Section 13.62(11p) lists governor as a partisan elective state office, §13.62(6) defines "elective state official" to include the governor, and §13.62(8) includes "the action of the governor in approving or vetoing any bill" within legislative action — so the governor is a lobbying target.
Section 13.62(2) defines "agency" to expressly include authorities created in subch. II of ch. 114 or in chs. 231, 232, 233, 234, 237, 238, or 279 — these are independent state authorities/agencies.

Section 13.62(10) defines lobbying as communications with elective state officials and legislative employees, and §13.62(8) defines legislative action to include actions by the legislature, either house, or any committee — covering the legislative branch.

Section 13.62(8m) defines "legislative employee" to include members/officers of the legislature, individuals employed under s. 13.20, and employees of legislative service agencies, and §13.62(10) makes communications with legislative employees lobbying.

Section 13.621(3) exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees acting in an official capacity from the registration/reporting requirements, indicating elected officials acting officially are not treated as lobbyist-actors under the statute.

Section 13.695(1) requires each agency to file a statement identifying officers and employees whose regular duties include attempting to influence legislative action, and §13.621(2) provides a separate exemption track for such agency lobbying — recognizing public employees as a distinct lobbying actor class.
Section 13.62(2) defines "agency" by enumerating state governmental bodies and specified statutory authorities; it contains no reference to ownership structure as a definitional criterion.
Section 13.62(2) defines "agency" through enumeration of governmental bodies and statutory authority chapters, without any reference to revenue source, funding structure, or financial criteria.
